newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Czech Prime Minister Klaus arrives in Malaysia.
newsitem.headline: Czech Prime Minister Klaus arrives in Malaysia.

text.p: Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus arrived in Malaysia on Sunday for a three-day official visit, as part of a tour of East Asian countries.
The national Bernama news agency said Klaus accompanied by his wife, Livia Klausova, and his delegation were received by Foreign Minister Abdullah Ahmad Badawi.
Klaus is scheduled to meet with Malaysia's King Tuanku Ja'afar and Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad on Monday.
He is also scheduled to deliver a keynote address at an economic seminar and attend a luncheon hosted by the National Chamber of Commerce and Industry.

In an interview with Bernama over the weekend, Czech ambassador to Malaysia, Jaroslav Olsa, said the republic could play a bridging role between Malaysian businessmen and Europe, due to its central location in Europe.

"The Czech republic is also developing free trade zones, which could benefit Malaysian export-oriented companies which want to use the republic as a redistribution base to other neighbouring countries," he said.
The republic is keen to participate in the second Asia-Europe meeting (ASEM) in London next year, Olsa said.
The first ASEM was held in Bangkok early this year but the Czech Republic was not among the 15 countries from Europe.
